findings.issue_text: Adding `force: true` to create_table for the already-existing top_topics migration can silently drop and recreate the table, destroying all top_topics data on environments that re-run the migration
Use of `String#scrub` in poll_feed.rb requires Ruby 2.1+, but the codebase runs on Ruby 1.9.3/2.0, causing NoMethodError and crashing the entire feed poll job

When request.referer is absent (browsers suppressing referer for iframe-initiated requests), URI('').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host raises InvalidAccess, so the 'loading' path in best can never be reached on first load for those users

loading.html.erb reloads every 30 seconds indefinitely with no failure state, re-enqueueing RetrieveTopic jobs forever when retrieval fails
Migration uses force: true on create_table :top_topics, dropping existing data on upgrade

force: true added to the pre-existing create_top_topics migration will drop and recreate top_topics, destroying aggregation data on installs that already ran it
Whitespace-only modifications to the unrelated MigrateWordCounts migration pollute the diff and appear to be accidental editor/tooling changes

RetrieveTopic enqueue passes the iframe viewer's current_user (usually nil) as user_id, a dead parameter that only controls throttling and implies user-scoped retrieval that the code does not enforce
The new embed.js (and embed.css.scss) is not referenced by any view, layout, or asset manifest and no admin setting exposes it, leaving the user-facing workflow unimplemented
Raw cook method skips sanitization for RSS/scraped content, enabling stored XSS in embed views via raw post.cooked
Request-triggered PollFeed job re-runs entire feed import in per-embed-request path, duplicating the hourly schedule and propagating network failures to the retrieval path
PollFeed loop lacks per-item error handling; one bad feed item (nil i.content in Atom feeds) permanently blocks subsequent items, especially with retry: false
embed.js origin check uses unanchored substring match (indexOf) instead of equality, allowing forged origins to pass
Referer header echoed unescaped into JS string literal in embed layout and used as postMessage targetOrigin, enabling script injection and hostile message delivery
feed_key cache key is dead code; no conditional GET/modified-since handling so every poll re-fetches and re-imports the full feed
TopicEmbed update branch uses embed.post without nil guard, causing permanent 500s for orphaned embeds, and title updates from changed feed entries are silently dropped

Disqus importer contract silently rewritten: removed method_option :category and PostCreator permalink call, replaced with TopicEmbed.import_remote, breaking -c option and changing behavior to full article scrape with lost category placement
Existing migration retroactively made destructive: create_table :top_topics changed to force: true, which silently drops and recreates the table with all rows lost on re-run
Early return for raw_html posts in app/models/post.rb:131 bypasses post_analyzer.cook and after_post_cook plugin filters, serving unfiltered remote HTML verbatim
skip_validations in post_revisor.rb disables all AR validations for any revise! caller, not just embeds, allowing invalid posts to persist
PollFeed scheduled job invoked synchronously and inline in topic_retriever.rb to service a single embed request, blocking and importing every feed item
Raw Referer header echoed into inline script in embed.html.erb with X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL enables XSS via crafted Referer
embeddable_host is a single exact-match string, preventing subdomains or multiple hosts from embedding, narrower than the stated validation system objective
Stored XSS via the raw_html cook path: feed/scraped content passes through Post#cook unsanitized and is rendered with raw post.cooked, allowing arbitrary script execution from a hostile feed source
Readability path only restricts tags/attributes to href/src on a/img, letting javascript: and data: URI values pass through untouched
SSRF/local file read: open(url) in import_remote executes before any scheme validation, so feed-supplied URLs like file:///etc/passwd or internal metadata endpoints are fetched by the server
Weak postMessage origin check in embed.js uses indexOf substring matching, which passes when e.origin is null/empty or merely appears anywhere in discourseUrl
Unescaped request.referer interpolated into an inline JS string in embed layout, allowing script injection into the embed page via crafted Referer header
poll_feed_spec.rb tests only verify method dispatch, not the new poll_feed behavior (RSS parsing, url fallback branch, CGI.unescapeHTML, TopicEmbed.import)
topic_retriever_spec.rb stubs out the redis throttle and perform_retrieve branches, leaving them untested
embed_controller_spec.rb retriever test mocks TopicRetriever entirely and never verifies the Jobs.enqueue arguments or render output
embed_controller_spec.rb 404 test can pass for the wrong reason because SiteSetting.embeddable_host is not stubbed, so the host check fails before params.require
topic_embed_spec.rb update-path test only asserts a regex match and never verifies content_sha1 persistence, dedup, or skip_validations; the identical-content no-op path is untested
force: true added to already-applied migration create_top_topics.rb risks silent irreversible data loss of the top_topics table
force: true on new topic_embeds table establishes same drop-if-exists hazard and bad pattern
topic_embeds.topic_id and post_id lack foreign key constraints, allowing orphaned rows after topic/post deletion
topic_embed.rb update path dereferences possibly-deleted post with no guard, risking NoMethodError mid-PollFeed loop
sidekiq retry: false on poll_feed.rb means one orphaned embed row silently kills all subsequent feed imports
No cleanup mechanism (dependent: :destroy or after_destroy hooks) for dangling topic_embeds rows, so orphan set grows
Unique index on embed_url lets a stale/dangling row permanently block re-import of that URL
cook_method default hard-coded as magic number 1 in SQL while enum lives in Ruby; enum reorder would silently reinterpret existing values

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adding `force: true` to create_table for the already-existing top_topics migration can silently drop and recreate the table, destroying all top_topics data on environments that re-run the migration

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists and then recreate it. While normal `db:migrate` won’t re-run an already-applied migration, any scenario that re-executes this migration against a DB where `top_topics` already exists (e.g., redo/reset patterns or atypical deployment/restore flows) can silently destroy existing `top_topics` data. This matches the finding and is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Use of `String#scrub` in poll_feed.rb requires Ruby 2.1+, but the codebase runs on Ruby 1.9.3/2.0, causing NoMethodError and crashing the entire feed poll job

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`. `String#scrub` is not available in older Rubies (commonly Ruby < 2.1), so this introduces a runtime compatibility risk where the feed poll job could raise `NoMethodError`. However, the diff itself does not state the project’s supported Ruby version, so the claim that it *will* break on Ruby 1.9.3/2.0 cannot be conclusively verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js and embed.css.scss are not reachable: no route, no config.assets.precompile entry, no copy to public/, so the /embed/best route 500s or breaks styling in production and embedding sites have no URL to load embed.js

adjudication.rationale: The new embed layout explicitly calls `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` (app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb), which in production Rails typically requires `embed.css` to be in the assets precompile list; this diff adds `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss` but does not add any `config.assets.precompile` entry. Similarly, `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` is introduced but nothing in the diff ensures it will be precompiled/served for third-party embedding. If the app uses default Rails precompile behavior, `/embed/best` can raise an asset-not-precompiled error (500) and embed.js may 404 in production.

adjudication_records.issue_text: When request.referer is absent (browsers suppressing referer for iframe-initiated requests), URI('').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host raises InvalidAccess, so the 'loading' path in best can never be reached on first load for those users

adjudication.rationale: EmbedController has `before_filter :ensure_embeddable`, which raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` when `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. If `request.referer` is nil/absent, `URI('')` yields a URI with `host == nil`, so the comparison is true (assuming `embeddable_host` is set) and the action errors before `best` can enqueue `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and `render 'loading'`. The controller spec explicitly asserts failure with no referer, confirming the loading path can’t be reached in that case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Imported HTML is never sanitized because the raw_html cook path returns raw content, skipping the Sanitize pipeline and enabling stored XSS from feed or scraped content

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, explicitly skipping the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (which is where Discourse typically sanitizes/filters HTML). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` using `contents` from RSS (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` + `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) or from `Readability::Document` (`doc.content`) without any sanitization shown in the diff. The embed view then renders `raw post.cooked`, so imported HTML is stored and served as-is, enabling stored XSS if feed/scraped content contains unsafe HTML/attributes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RSS 2.0 feeds crash the poller with NoMethodError since i.content is nil for RSS (only Atom has content), and retry: false silently disables import forever
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that RSS feeds lack `i.content`, causing a NoMethodError when `i.content` is nil, which matches the golden issue about `i.content.scrub` assuming content is always present and needing a fallback (e.g., description). Extra mention about `retry: false` is additional but does not change the core match.

adjudication_records.issue_text: loading.html.erb reloads every 30 seconds indefinitely with no failure state, re-enqueueing RetrieveTopic jobs forever when retrieval fails

adjudication.rationale: `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` unconditionally reloads the page every 30s (`setTimeout(... document.location.reload())`) with no stop/failure condition. In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil it always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading`. If retrieval never succeeds (e.g., `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` returns early because `SiteSetting.embed_by_username` is unset or user not found, network errors, etc.), the page will keep reloading and each reload will enqueue another `retrieve_topic` job, leading to potentially unbounded job queue growth.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration uses force: true on create_table :top_topics, dropping existing data on upgrade

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the migration `CreateTopTopics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` (db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb). In Rails, `force: true` drops the table if it already exists before recreating it, which can delete existing `top_topics` data during migration/upgrade. This is exactly the data-loss risk described in the finding and is introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Referer-host equality check in embed_controller is brittle (www/subdomain mismatch) and the embeddable_host setting has two consumers with different, undocumented semantics

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, embedding is allowed only when `URI(request.referer || '').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (strict string equality). This will reject common valid cases like `www.example.com` vs `example.com` or other subdomain variations even if the admin intends to allow the whole site, making the new embed feature fail unexpectedly. Additionally, `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` is also used in `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` to validate the *embed_url* host, meaning the same setting gates two different inputs (referer host vs embed_url host) without any indication in `site_settings.yml`/locales, which can lead to misconfiguration and broken behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Update path assumes embed.post is present; a deleted post causes NoMethodError in PostRevisor and permanently blocks the feed poll

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally constructs `PostRevisor.new(post)` when the content hash changes. If the associated `posts` row has been deleted (possible despite `topic_embeds.post_id null: false`, since there’s no FK/`dependent` behavior shown), `embed.post` will be `nil` and `PostRevisor.new(nil)` / later `@post.save` will raise, breaking the polling/import flow. `Jobs::PollFeed` has `sidekiq_options retry: false` and no rescue, so a single bad embed can repeatedly cause the scheduled job to fail on future runs as well.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Relative URL to absolute conversion only handles leading-slash forms, leaving relative (page2.html), protocol-relative (//cdn...), and non-default-port URLs broken

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, links/images are only rewritten when `href`/`src` starts with `'/'`. That means relative paths like `page2.html` are left untouched, and protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn...` incorrectly match `start_with?('/')` and get rewritten to something like `#{prefix}/cdn...` (wrong host). However, the finding’s claim about “non-default-port URLs” is not supported because `prefix` explicitly appends `:#{uri.port}` when the port is not 80/443.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The Disqus importer was rewritten to call TopicEmbed.import_remote, silently deleting the method_option :category (-c) feature

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes the Disqus Thor task option `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` and the associated `category_id` lookup, and replaces topic creation via `PostCreator.new(..., category: category_id)` with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which does not accept/apply a category. This is a behavior regression: the `-c` feature is deleted with no replacement or warning.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The Disqus importer changes the created topic from a permalink post to a full readability-scraped article import, unrelated to the stated intent

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the Disqus importer’s topic-creation behavior changed materially: it no longer creates an initial post containing only a permalink (`PostCreator.new(... raw: "\[[Permalink](#{t[:link]})\]" ...)`) and instead calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which uses `ruby-readability` to fetch and embed the full remote article content (`Readability::Document.new(open(url).read ...)` then `TopicEmbed.import(... doc.content)`). That is a real, nontrivial scope/behavior change within the Disqus importer unrelated to the surrounding “feed importing and embedding” additions, and merits review even if not strictly a defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: force: true added to the pre-existing create_top_topics migration will drop and recreate top_topics, destroying aggregation data on installs that already ran it

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, which would drop/recreate the table *if this migration is executed when the table already exists*. However, the finding’s specific claim that this will destroy data "on installs that already ran it" is not supported by the diff: Rails will not re-run an already-applied migration during a normal upgrade, so existing installs that have this migration recorded in `schema_migrations` would not execute the altered `create_table` again.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Whitespace-only modifications to the unrelated MigrateWordCounts migration pollute the diff and appear to be accidental editor/tooling changes

adjudication.rationale: The diff for `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` only adjusts whitespace (removing trailing spaces on a blank line) and changes the file’s newline-at-EOF status. This is a verifiable, whitespace-only formatting change and does not introduce or expose a functional defect or substantive review issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated deletion of a blank line in post_revisor.rb's revise! mixes cosmetic churn into the feature diff

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `lib/post_revisor.rb` does remove a blank line inside `revise!`, but that is purely cosmetic churn (formatting) and not a substantive review issue under the provided categories (it introduces no behavior change or actionable non-bug concern).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The retrieval throttle's no_throttle is keyed off the viewing user rather than the embed owner, so any staff member viewing the embed page bypasses the 60-second throttle and triggers a synchronous HTTP fetch of a third-party page

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::RetrieveTopic, the throttle bypass is set from the *viewer* (args[:user_id]) via `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)`, and in TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently? that completely disables the 60s throttle (`return false if @opts[:no_throttle]`). The actual HTTP fetch is performed in `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` via `TopicEmbed.import_remote(... open(url).read ...)`, but this happens inside the background job, not synchronously in the controller request (EmbedController enqueues the job and renders loading). So the core concern (staff can cause repeated fetches) is real and diff-grounded, but it's more of a design/perf/safety issue than a clearly unintended defect, and the “synchronous” part is overstated for the web request path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RetrieveTopic enqueue passes the iframe viewer's current_user (usually nil) as user_id, a dead parameter that only controls throttling and implies user-scoped retrieval that the code does not enforce

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, the job is enqueued with `user_id: current_user.try(:id)` (often nil for an embed iframe), and in `Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute` that `user_id` is only used to look up the user to set `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)` when constructing `TopicRetriever`. Retrieval/throttling in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` is keyed only by `@embed_url` (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), not per-user, so passing a viewer `user_id` can be misleading and provides no user-scoped enforcement beyond the staff throttle bypass. This is a valid design/scope concern but not a functional defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new embed.js (and embed.css.scss) is not referenced by any view, layout, or asset manifest and no admin setting exposes it, leaving the user-facing workflow unimplemented

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the diff: `embed.css.scss` *is* referenced by `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb` via `<%= stylesheet_link_tag 'embed' %>`, so it isn’t unreferenced. `embed.js` is not included by any Rails view/layout in this diff, but it plausibly exists to be loaded directly by external sites (to create the iframe) and the diff doesn’t show the asset precompile/manifest configuration needed to verify it’s inaccessible. Therefore the claim that both assets are unused and the workflow is unimplemented is not verifiable from the diff and is partly false.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Raw cook method skips sanitization for RSS/scraped content, enabling stored XSS in embed views via raw post.cooked

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `Post.cook` early-returning `raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html` (app/models/post.rb), explicitly skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. Feed/scraped imports set this mode (`TopicEmbed.import` passes `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`) and accept untrusted HTML from RSS (`Jobs::PollFeed` uses `i.content` with only `CGI.unescapeHTML(...scrub)`), then the embed view renders it directly via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). This creates a verifiable stored XSS path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Request-triggered PollFeed job re-runs entire feed import in per-embed-request path, duplicating the hourly schedule and propagating network failures to the retrieval path

adjudication.rationale: Verified: TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` whenever `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true (lib/topic_retriever.rb), meaning a request-triggered embed retrieval can synchronously re-run the full feed polling/import logic (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) despite that job also being scheduled hourly. PollFeed performs network I/O via `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` without rescue, so failures can bubble up and abort the per-embed retrieval attempt. This is a concrete architecture/reliability concern grounded in the diff, though not necessarily a strict functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed loop lacks per-item error handling; one bad feed item (nil i.content in Atom feeds) permanently blocks subsequent items, especially with retry: false

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item has `i.content == nil` (plausible for some Atom/RSS variants), this will raise `NoMethodError` on `nil.scrub`, aborting the entire `rss.items.each` processing and preventing subsequent items from being imported in that run. There is no per-item rescue, and `sidekiq_options retry: false` means a failure won’t be retried, so items after the bad one are skipped until the next scheduled run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js origin check uses unanchored substring match (indexOf) instead of equality, allowing forged origins to pass
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same flaw: origin validation uses indexOf/substring matching rather than strict equality or proper parsing, so a malicious domain containing the trusted domain as a substring (e.g., evil-discourseUrl.com) can bypass the check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Referer header echoed unescaped into JS string literal in embed layout and used as postMessage targetOrigin, enabling script injection and hostile message delivery
feed_key cache key is dead code; no conditional GET/modified-since handling so every poll re-fetches and re-imports the full feed

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` is defined but never referenced anywhere in the diff, so it’s dead code. Also `poll_feed` always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and then iterates every `rss.items` on each run; there’s no use of `If-Modified-Since`/ETag or any cached last-modified value to avoid re-fetching/processing the whole feed. While `TopicEmbed.import` avoids rewriting unchanged posts via `content_sha1`, the job still re-downloads and re-processes all items each poll.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed update branch uses embed.post without nil guard, causing permanent 500s for orphaned embeds, and title updates from changed feed entries are silently dropped

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update branch does `post = embed.post` with no nil handling. If a `topic_embeds` row becomes orphaned (no FK; `post` deleted), then on content change it will call `PostRevisor.new(post)` with `post == nil`, which will raise and can 500 during feed polling/retrieval. Also, the update path revises only the post raw (`revisor.revise!`) and never updates the topic title, so changed feed titles are ignored.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus importer contract silently rewritten: removed method_option :category and PostCreator permalink call, replaced with TopicEmbed.import_remote, breaking -c option and changing behavior to full article scrape with lost category placement

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and deletes all logic that maps `options[:category]` to a `category_id` passed into `PostCreator`. It also replaces the old `PostCreator.new(..., raw: "[[Permalink](...)]", ..., category: category_id)` call with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which no longer accepts/uses a category and changes imported content from a permalink stub to a remote readability scrape. This is a verifiable breaking behavior change for anyone using `-c` and for category placement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Existing migration retroactively made destructive: create_table :top_topics changed to force: true, which silently drops and recreates the table with all rows lost on re-run

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration (20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb) from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` drops the table if it already exists before recreating it, which would silently delete all rows if this migration is re-run (e.g., in `db:migrate:redo` / recreating environments). This is a destructive behavior introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Early return for raw_html posts in app/models/post.rb:131 bypasses post_analyzer.cook and after_post_cook plugin filters, serving unfiltered remote HTML verbatim

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post.cook_methods` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which skips `post_analyzer.cook(*args)` and `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`. New code paths set this mode for imported remote content (e.g., `TopicEmbed.import` passes `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and the embed view renders `raw post.cooked`). This means imported HTML can bypass the normal cooking/sanitization and post-cook plugin filtering and be served verbatim, creating an XSS/security defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: skip_validations in post_revisor.rb disables all AR validations for any revise! caller, not just embeds, allowing invalid posts to persist

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `PostRevisor#update_post` from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, meaning any caller of `revise!` that passes `skip_validations: true` will bypass all ActiveRecord validations. The new embed update path (`TopicEmbed.import` calling `revisor.revise!(..., skip_validations: true, ...)`) uses this, and the mechanism is not scoped to embeds. However, it’s opt-in via `@opts` and the diff doesn’t show untrusted/external callers setting it, so it’s more of a design/scope risk than a verifiable defect on its own.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed scheduled job invoked synchronously and inline in topic_retriever.rb to service a single embed request, blocking and importing every feed item

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#perform_retrieve, when SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline before falling back to HTTP fetch. PollFeed#poll_feed (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) fetches the configured feed and iterates `rss.items.each` importing each item via `TopicEmbed.import`, so a single embed retrieval can trigger a full feed import synchronously in that code path. However, the embed controller enqueues `:retrieve_topic` (EmbedController#best) rather than running TopicRetriever in the web request, so it blocks that retrieval job rather than the immediate HTTP response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Raw Referer header echoed into inline script in embed.html.erb with X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL enables XSS via crafted Referer

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb` the Referer is interpolated as `<%= request.referer %>` inside a JS string, but Rails ERB output is HTML-escaped by default (so characters like `'`, `<`, `</script>` won’t break out into executable script). Additionally, `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` validates `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, so an arbitrary attacker-controlled Referer from another origin is rejected. The diff does set `X-Frame-Options = ALLOWALL`, but the specific claim of XSS via crafted Referer is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embeddable_host is a single exact-match string, preventing subdomains or multiple hosts from embedding, narrower than the stated validation system objective

adjudication.rationale: The diff enforces embedding eligibility via exact string equality against a single `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` value: `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` requires `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` requires `URI(@embed_url).host` to equal that same setting. This makes it impossible to permit multiple allowed hosts or wildcard/subdomain matching without code changes. It’s a real limitation introduced by this implementation, but not a verifiable defect given the setting text says singular “Host that can embed…”.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS via the raw_html cook path: feed/scraped content passes through Post#cook unsanitized and is rendered with raw post.cooked, allowing arbitrary script execution from a hostile feed source

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a `raw_html` cook path that bypasses the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline: `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb). Feed/RSS import uses this path by creating posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` and `skip_validations: true` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), and `Jobs::PollFeed` takes `i.content` from the feed (only `CGI.unescapeHTML(...scrub)`, no HTML sanitization) and passes it into `TopicEmbed.import`. The embed view renders `post.cooked` with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). As a result, hostile feed content containing `<script>` or other dangerous HTML would be stored and rendered unsanitized, enabling stored XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Readability path only restricts tags/attributes to href/src on a/img, letting javascript: and data: URI values pass through untouched

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, `Readability::Document.new` is configured to allow tags including `a` and `img` and attributes `%w[href src]` (lib/models/topic_embed.rb). The diff shows no sanitization of attribute *values* (e.g., `href="javascript:..."` or `src="data:..."`). The resulting `doc.content` is passed into `TopicEmbed.import`, then saved via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, causing `Post#cook` to `return raw` (app/models/post.rb). Finally, the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). `absolutize_urls` only rewrites relative URLs starting with `/` and does not filter dangerous schemes. This is a verifiable XSS risk introduced by the raw HTML path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SSRF/local file read: open(url) in import_remote executes before any scheme validation, so feed-supplied URLs like file:///etc/passwd or internal metadata endpoints are fetched by the server

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s feed path (`Jobs::PollFeed`) does not call `import_remote`; it calls `TopicEmbed.import`, which immediately returns unless `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, so `file:///etc/passwd` (or other non-http(s) schemes) are rejected before any fetch. The web-triggered embed retrieval path enqueues `TopicRetriever`, which refuses to fetch unless `URI(@embed_url).host` matches `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`; `file://` URLs have no host and will be treated as invalid. While `TopicEmbed.import_remote` itself does `open(url).read` before the later http(s) regex check in `import`, the finding’s specific claim about “feed-supplied URLs like file:///etc/passwd” being fetched by the server is not supported by the diff’s call sites.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Weak postMessage origin check in embed.js uses indexOf substring matching, which passes when e.origin is null/empty or merely appears anywhere in discourseUrl

adjudication.rationale: In new `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the origin validation is `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`, which is a substring match rather than an exact origin comparison. This can incorrectly accept messages from other origins whose `e.origin` is contained within `discourseUrl` (e.g., discourseUrl `https://forum.example.com.attacker.tld/` would accept origin `https://forum.example.com`). That weakens the postMessage security check for the resize handler.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unescaped request.referer interpolated into an inline JS string in embed layout, allowing script injection into the embed page via crafted Referer header
matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same vulnerability: the Referer header (request.referer) is interpolated into inline JavaScript without escaping, enabling XSS/script injection via a crafted Referer value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed_spec.rb tests only verify method dispatch, not the new poll_feed behavior (RSS parsing, url fallback branch, CGI.unescapeHTML, TopicEmbed.import)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantive logic in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb#poll_feed` (requires `simple-rss`, parses `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`, iterates `rss.items`, URL fallback to `i.id` when `i.link` is blank/invalid, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and calls `TopicEmbed.import`). However `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only asserts `execute` preconditions and that `execute` delegates to `poll_feed` (via `poller.expects(:poll_feed)`), without any coverage of the new parsing/branching/import behavior. This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap rather than a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_retriever_spec.rb stubs out the redis throttle and perform_retrieve branches, leaving them untested

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb`, the “valid host” examples stub `retrieved_recently?` (`topic_retriever.expects(:retrieved_recently?).returns(false/true)`) and only assert whether `perform_retrieve` is called, without exercising the real Redis throttle logic implemented in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` (uses `$redis.setnx`/`expire`). Likewise, the spec never executes the internals of `perform_retrieve` (feed polling branch, `fetch_http`, `TopicEmbed` existence checks), so those new branches remain untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller_spec.rb retriever test mocks TopicRetriever entirely and never verifies the Jobs.enqueue arguments or render output

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, the example "tells the topic retriever to work when no previous embed is found" stubs TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed to nil and then mocks TopicRetriever.new and expects retriever.retrieve, but the controller implementation actually calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: embed_url) and renders 'loading' when no topic_id is found (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). The spec does not assert the enqueue arguments nor that the 'loading' template is rendered, so it is not validating the behavior introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller_spec.rb 404 test can pass for the wrong reason because SiteSetting.embeddable_host is not stubbed, so the host check fails before params.require

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, the `before_filter :ensure_embeddable` runs before `embed_url = params.require(:embed_url)`. `ensure_embeddable` raises if `SiteSetting.embeddable_host.blank?` (or referer host mismatch), so the spec `it "is 404 without an embed_url"` (which does not stub `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`) can fail early due to the embeddable host check rather than exercising the missing-parameter path. This is a real, diff-grounded test weakness, not a production defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed_spec.rb update-path test only asserts a regex match and never verifies content_sha1 persistence, dedup, or skip_validations; the identical-content no-op path is untested

adjudication.rationale: In spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb, the update-path example (`it "Supports updating the post"`) only asserts `post.cooked` matches `/new contents/` after calling `TopicEmbed.import` with changed contents. It does not verify that the associated `TopicEmbed` row’s `content_sha1` is updated (`embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)`), that the unique `embed_url` dedup behavior is preserved (no extra `TopicEmbed` rows created), nor that the no-op path when `content_sha1` is unchanged is exercised (the `if content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1` branch). The mention of `skip_validations` is also diff-grounded: import sets `skip_validations: true` for both `PostCreator` and `PostRevisor`, and `PostRevisor` now conditionally validates via `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, but the spec doesn’t assert this behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: force: true added to already-applied migration create_top_topics.rb risks silent irreversible data loss of the top_topics table

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` from `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it, which can silently destroy any `top_topics` data if this migration is ever re-run (e.g., `db:migrate:redo`, `db:reset` against a DB that already has the table, or other nonstandard migration states). It’s not a guaranteed production defect since applied migrations typically aren’t re-executed, but it’s a concrete, diff-grounded risk worth flagging.

adjudication_records.issue_text: force: true on new topic_embeds table establishes same drop-if-exists hazard and bad pattern

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb` uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, which in Rails will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it. Since this is a *new* table in this diff, it likely won’t drop anything in the normal forward-migration path, but it is a risky pattern that can cause data loss in abnormal/partial states (e.g., if the table exists due to a previous run or manual creation). The finding is accurately grounded in the diff and is actionable, but it’s not a guaranteed defect in typical use.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embeds.topic_id and post_id lack foreign key constraints, allowing orphaned rows after topic/post deletion

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb the table defines `t.integer :topic_id` and `t.integer :post_id` (both `null: false`) but only adds an index on `embed_url`; there are no `add_foreign_key` statements to enforce referential integrity to `topics`/`posts`. This can allow orphaned `topic_embeds` rows if the associated topic/post is deleted, but the diff does not show actual broken behavior—it's a schema integrity improvement request rather than a directly verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb update path dereferences possibly-deleted post with no guard, risking NoMethodError mid-PollFeed loop

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, when an embed already exists it does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally passes `post` into `PostRevisor.new(post)` and later returns `post`. If the associated post has been deleted (possible since the migration adds `post_id` but no foreign key constraint), `embed.post` can be nil, causing errors (e.g., in PostRevisor) and potentially breaking the PollFeed `rss.items.each` loop.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sidekiq retry: false on poll_feed.rb means one orphaned embed row silently kills all subsequent feed imports

adjudication.rationale: The diff does set `sidekiq_options retry: false` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, but nothing here shows that an “orphaned embed row” is created or that such a row would “silently kill all subsequent feed imports.” `TopicEmbed.import` only creates a `topic_embeds` row if `creator.create` returns a post, and it’s wrapped in a transaction, so it won’t create a lone embed row on a failed post creation. Also, a failure in `poll_feed` would raise and fail the job (not silently), and future scheduled runs would still be enqueued hourly regardless of Sidekiq retry behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No cleanup mechanism (dependent: :destroy or after_destroy hooks) for dangling topic_embeds rows, so orphan set grows

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `topic_embeds` with required `topic_id`/`post_id` (migration `create_topic_embeds`) and a `TopicEmbed` model that only declares `belongs_to :topic` / `belongs_to :post` without any `dependent` behavior (and the diff does not add corresponding `has_one/has_many ... dependent: :destroy` on `Topic` or `Post`, nor any `after_destroy` cleanup). So if a Topic or Post is deleted, the associated `topic_embeds` row would not be automatically removed, potentially leaving orphan rows that accumulate.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unique index on embed_url lets a stale/dangling row permanently block re-import of that URL

adjudication.rationale: The migration adds `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`, and `TopicEmbed.import` treats the presence of an existing row (`embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`) as authoritative, taking the update path instead of creating a new topic/post. There is no handling for an orphaned `topic_embeds` row (e.g., if the associated `post`/`topic` was deleted later; `belongs_to` has no `dependent:` cleanup and no DB FK shown). In that case, the unique index prevents inserting a replacement row for the same `embed_url`, and the code would also likely fail on `PostRevisor.new(post)` when `embed.post` is nil, effectively blocking re-import for that URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: cook_method default hard-coded as magic number 1 in SQL while enum lives in Ruby; enum reorder would silently reinterpret existing values

adjudication.rationale: The migration hard-codes `default: 1` for `posts.cook_method` (db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb) while the meaning of values is defined in Ruby via `Post.cook_methods ||= Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` (app/models/post.rb). The diff doesn’t show any shared constant tying `1` to `:regular`, so future reordering/changes to the enum could silently change how existing rows are interpreted. This is a maintainability/data-compat concern grounded in the diff, not an immediate, demonstrable runtime defect.
